account: Residents of Bade District, Taoyuan, complained in the Facebook group 記憶八德. A white BMW with a loud exhaust kept roaring down Jieshou Road late at night. The Taoyuan City Department of Environmental Protection received the complaint on the night of 22 April 2025. Its Quiet Taoyuan (靜桃) task force immediately set up AI sound camera equipment at the relevant spots. By analyzing the noise data against the complaints, it worked out where and when the car appeared. On 23 April environmental and police officers stopped it near Daxing Road. The car was referred to the motor vehicle office for a modification review. The reports said that a fine of up to NT$3,600 under the Noise Control Act and an improvement order would follow. All five cited reports reproduce statements from the Taoyuan City Department of Environmental Protection, and none adds reporting of its own. In January 2026 the bureau said that noise complaints had fallen 38 percent since the Quiet Taoyuan project began. The bureau also reported that 50 sound-camera sets were installed across the city.

ai_role.statement: The bureau's own description is the only account of the system's contribution. The task force placed AI sound camera equipment at the relevant locations on the night of the complaint. Analysis of the noise data with the complaint reports gave the car's haunts and times. Environmental and police officers then found it near Daxing Road on 23 April. The sources do not say how the cameras tie noise to a vehicle. They report no decibel reading. They give no counterfactual for how long a conventional patrol would have taken. The stop, the referral and the pending penalty were the officers' work.

fields.account: Residents of Bade District, Taoyuan, complained in the Facebook group 記憶八德. A white BMW with a loud exhaust kept roaring down Jieshou Road late at night. The Taoyuan City Department of Environmental Protection received the complaint on the night of 22 April 2025. Its Quiet Taoyuan (靜桃) task force immediately set up AI sound camera equipment at the relevant spots. By analyzing the noise data against the complaints, it worked out where and when the car appeared. On 23 April environmental and police officers stopped it near Daxing Road. The car was referred to the motor vehicle office for a modification review. The reports said that a fine of up to NT$3,600 under the Noise Control Act and an improvement order would follow. All five cited reports reproduce statements from the Taoyuan City Department of Environmental Protection, and none adds reporting of its own. In January 2026 the bureau said that noise complaints had fallen 38 percent since the Quiet Taoyuan project began. The bureau also reported that 50 sound-camera sets were installed across the city.
